findings.finding: Q3 volume is already guided down: the company told the market on 2026-07-23 that Q3 shipments would decline low to mid-single digits, depletions were -6% in Q2 and -5% for the 29 weeks to 2026-07-18, and the CFO said volume was tracking to the LOW end of the FY range (down low- to mid-single digits); consensus revenue of $523M (-2.7% y/y) sits roughly at shipments -4% plus 1-2% price, so the likely print is in line on revenue and the risk is a volume-guide narrowing to 'mid-single-digit decline'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23): depletions -6%, guide maintained, stock +3.23% close-to-close; Q1 2026 (2026-04-30) -9.59%; Q3 2025 shipments -13.7% with GM +450bp and raised EPS guide, +5.45%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is the company's own guide and consensus revenue already embeds it. What is not priced is whether the 2026-10-22 release narrows the volume range to its low end; a stock that had priced that would not have run +15.7% in 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: CFO comment that volume tracks the low end is from the call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-boston-beer-q2-2026-shares-slip-after-mixed-results-93CH-4810200); same company source, counted once.

findings.finding: Category scans stayed weak through the Q3 quarter-end: Circana 12 weeks through 2026-09-27 show total US retail beverage alcohol dollar sales -0.9% with beer the larger drag, off-premise bev-alc -2.2% in the week to 2026-08-02 with Circana projecting softness through Labor Day, and FMB (Twisted Tea's category) at -4% dollars / -6.4% cases on the 52 weeks to 2026-04-19; nothing in the public scans shows the Twisted Tea stabilisation that Bernstein and UBS say they need.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Depletion misses have mattered when they moved the guide (Q1 2026 -9.59%); Q2 2026 depletions -6% with guide held got +3.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry series are visible to the sell-side (RBC's 2026-10-20 note cites Nielsen and persistent volume softness), so this is largely priced; what is not priced is any Boston Beer-specific depletion number for Aug-Sep, which only the release gives. If the market had priced a weak Q3 depletion print the stock would not be at its mean target after a 15% run.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Early-August scan read: https://cpgintelligence.ai/takes/off-premise-beer-sales-down-22-in-early-august-and-circana-beer-2026-08-17 ; RBC 'underperformance unlikely to change on Q3' (persistent volume softness, higher freight): https://www.marketscreener.com/news/boston-beer-s-stock-underperformance-unlikely-to-change-on-q3-results-rbc-says-ce785cd8da8bf625 (2026-10-20). findings.finding: Constellation Brands, reporting after Boston Beer last spoke, showed beer depletions -0.6% for June-August 2026 against expectations of flat to slightly positive while shipments ran +5.5% on distributor restocking, and its shares fell about 5%: a peer read that summer US beer demand stayed soft into Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history; SAM's moves track its own depletion/guide line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 2026-10-07 and SAM rose ~15% afterwards, so the market read it as not transmitting to SAM; STZ's weakness is concentrated in the Hispanic consumer and imported lager, a different segment from FMB/hard tea. Small residual.
findings.independence: Second STZ source: https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/08/constellation-brands-fy2027-q2-earnings-analysis (2026-10-08). Shares the category direction of the Circana finding but is a separate company document.

findings.finding: Aluminium came off its peak before Q3: LME hit $3,855/t on 2026-06-02 and was $3,105.50/t on 2026-06-30 (H1 2026 average $3,386, +33.4% y/y; US Midwest premium averaged ~109 c/lb in H1); management said in July it does not hedge commodities and could revise the EPS outlook if commodity inflation kept rising, so a lower Q3 spot than the July-guide spot reduces the risk of a commodity-driven EPS cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: GM +450bp and raised EPS guide (incl. lower tariff cost), stock +5.45%; GM low end raised in Q2 2026 with stock +3.23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Commodity-to-company transmission with can-contract lags is not modelled in the published previews, which talk about volume; if the market had priced relief the EPS consensus would have risen, but it fell 3.1% over two months (Investing.com 2026-10-22). Q3 aluminium and Midwest premium levels are not sourced, so this is a proxy.
findings.independence: Management's 'could revise if commodity inflation keeps rising / no hedging' is from the Q2 call summary (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-boston-beer-q2-2026-shares-slip-after-mixed-results-93CH-4810200). RBC cites higher freight costs continuing into 2027 (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/boston-beer-s-stock-underperformance-unlikely-to-change-on-q3-results-rbc-says-ce785cd8da8bf625), which cuts the other way on input costs.

findings.finding: The July guide built EPS levers to hold $8.50-$10.50 at low-end volume: GM low end raised to 48.5% (from 48%), incremental A&P cut to $0-20M (from $20-40M) with Q4 advertising guided down y/y, capex cut to $60-80M, and the CFO said low-end volume 'does not necessarily' mean low-end EPS; a reaffirmed EPS range with a narrowed volume range is the likely guide shape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS missed consensus by ~24% ($3.65 vs $4.83) but guide maintained with GM raised and stock rose +3.23% — this name pays for the guide, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the levers are public. The FY EPS consensus is dispersed ($8.99-$9.59) under a $9.50 midpoint, so a reaffirmation is not fully in the bar; with the stock at its mean PT after a 15% run, a mere reaffirmation may already be in the price.
findings.independence: Same primary document as the volume finding (different lines of it); CFO quote from https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-boston-beer-q2-2026-shares-slip-after-mixed-results-93CH-4810200.

findings.finding: Q3 laps the toughest margin comparison of the year: Q3 2025 gross margin was 50.8% (+450bp) with A&P +$16.8M, and management guided that Q4, not Q3, carries the largest y/y GM rate improvement while H2 advertising is up y/y overall and Q4 down, implying Q3 A&P is up y/y; with tariffs ($20-30M FY) and aluminium/freight inflation, flat EPS ($4.22 vs $4.25) has little cushion and the trailing four-quarter EPS surprise averages -3.4% (last quarter -23.5%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS miss of ~24% with guide held: stock +3.23%. The quarter's EPS has not driven this name's reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS was cut 3.1% over two months, so some of this is in the bar; the remaining risk is a second consecutive EPS miss that the reaction history says the stock looks through if the guide holds.
findings.independence: Guide phasing from https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-boston-beer-q2-2026-shares-slip-after-mixed-results-93CH-4810200 ; surprise history from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/boston-beers-q3-earnings-horizon-135100163.html.
